question: Shared: MCI vs normal controls from ADNI resting-state fMRI (116-ROI AAL), binary SVM classification in both. P-516 (Guo et al., Front Neurosci 2021) builds higher-order networks PCn by iterating Pearson correlation and tests whether higher order adds discrimination; 143 participants (299 scans), subject-level 5-fold CV. P-523 (Li et al., Front Cell Dev Biol 2021) combines three first-order estimators (Pearson, sparse representation, Granger causality) by multi-kernel learning; 63 MCI / 64 NC, nested LOOCV. Features and validation differ, which condition 1 allows.

figures.P-516: No accuracy is printed as a number; all accuracies appear only in Figures 6, 7 and 9. The text states that the accuracy of the convergent network (PCconv, thirty iterations) approaches 50%; the captions state that accuracy decreases with n in all cases (Figure 6) and that SEN and SPE of PC1 (ordinary Pearson) are better than the other cases (Figure 7), so PC1 is P-516's best network. Illustrative Wilson for 0.50 at n = 143 subjects: [0.419, 0.581].
figures.P-523: Nested LOOCV, 127 participants: MCPC 87.40% (111/127), Wilson [0.805, 0.921], AUC 0.922; single Pearson (PC) 77.95% (99/127), Wilson [0.700, 0.843], AUC 0.851; SR 81.10%; GCM 72.44%.

matched_figure_check: P-516's own figures account for the recorded gap. Its accuracy falls from the first-order Pearson network (PC1, its best) toward 50% as the order n rises, in all cases, and P-516 states that at convergence the discrimination almost disappears; the recorded 50% is the end point of that deliberate iteration. A paper therefore shows that the feature construction produces the gap, which is a condition-3 failure. The matched condition, first-order Pearson connectivity, exists in both papers (P-516 PC1; P-523 PC 77.95%), but P-516 prints PC1's accuracy only in figures, so no numeric matched comparison can be made.
performance_validity: Not triggered: P-523's 87.40% (AUC 0.922) is below 0.97, and P-516's recorded value is about 50%. The recorded P-516 value is an ablation end point, not a best-performance claim.
reason: The record takes the end point of P-516's ablation, the convergent higher-order network whose accuracy approaches 50%, as P-516's result, while P-516's best network is ordinary first-order Pearson correlation (condition 6). P-516's own figures show that the iteration drives the accuracy down to chance, so a paper shows the explanation is sufficient (condition 3). On the first-order Pearson condition both papers share, P-516 prints no number to set against P-523's 77.95%.
